statement.p: Find \int_C((x^2+2 y)\vec i + y^3\vec j)\cdot d\vec r where C consists of the three line segments from (2,0,0) to (2,5,0) to (0,5,0) to (0,5,3).

p.m: \int_C((x^2+2 y)\vec i + y^3\vec j)\cdot d\vec r =

static.solution: \vec F = (x^2+2 y)\vec i + y^3\vec j, the line integral along the third segment, which is parallel to the z-axis, is zero. On the first segment, which is parallel to the y-axis, only the \vec j-component contributes. On the second segment, which is parallel to the x-axis, only the \vec i-component contributes. On the first segment x=2 and y varies from 0 to 5; on the second segment y=5 and x varies from 2 to 0. Thus, we have \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^{5} ((2^2+2 y)\vec i + y^3\vec j) \cdot \vec j\, dy + \int_{2}^0 ((x^2+10)\vec i + 125\vec j)\cdot \vec i \, dx = \int_0^{5} y^3\,dy + \int_2^0 (x^2+10)\,dx = 0\, y^4\Big|_0^{5} - \left(\frac{x^3}{3} + 10 x\right)\Big|_0^2 = \frac{1603}{12}
